title: Smooth source pullback of oriented nearby cycles
statement: Let $S$ be Noetherian and $X\xrightarrow{h}Y\xrightarrow{g}S$ morphisms of finite presentation with $h$ smooth, and put $f=gh$. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring killed by an integer invertible on $S$. Write $\bar h:V_f\to V_g$ for the morphism induced by $(h,1_S)$ in [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles]. For every $L\in D^b_c(Y_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], the ordinary counit-defined comparison $\bar h^*R\Psi_gL\to R\Psi_f h^*L$ is an isomorphism. It is an isomorphism of objects on the vanishing topos, not only of sliced comparison cones, and imposes no $\Psi$-goodness hypothesis. The comparison is compatible with ordinary nearby-cycle comparisons for further Cartesian base changes of $S$.

source.place: Section 9.3, printed p. 22, smooth source calculation on the smooth locus of the last semistable curve; smooth source functoriality used there.

proof.text: The universal property of the oriented product [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] applied to the projections $hp'_1$ and $p'_2$ and the composite 2-morphism gives the morphism $\bar h:V_f\to V_g$ and the canonical identification $\bar h\psi_f\simeq\psi_g h$. The counit mate of this identification is exactly the comparison displayed in the statement, by the definition of $R\Psi$ and of the ordinary comparison in [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles]. Smoothness and finite presentation of $h$ persist after every base change, and the coefficient annihilator remains invertible, so all later strict-local diagrams have the same hypotheses.

source.place: Expose XI, 1.4--1.5: functoriality of the vanishing topos and the base-change comparison as a mate.

proof.text: Fix an oriented-product point $z=z_{x,t,c}$ of $V_f$ [lem-trf-oriented-product-points-conservative]: a geometric point $x$ of $X$, a geometric point $t$ of $S$, and a specialization $c:S_{(t)}\to S_{(s)}$ with $s=f(x)$. Put $y=h(x)$. Since $p_1\bar h=hp'_1$ and $p_2\bar h=p'_2$ compatibly with the $2$-morphisms, the universal property [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] gives $\bar h z\simeq z_{y,t,c}$, the corresponding point of $V_g$. Applying the point-cohomology formula [lem-trf-oriented-point-cohomology] with the second factor $1_S$ (so the strict localization of the second factor at $t$ is $S_{(t)}$), $z^*\bar h^*R\Psi_gL\simeq z_{y,t,c}^*R\Psi_gL\simeq R\Gamma(Y_{(y)}\times_{S_{(s)}}S_{(t)},L)$ and $z^*R\Psi_fh^*L\simeq R\Gamma(X_{(x)}\times_{S_{(s)}}S_{(t)},h^*L)$, the fibre products formed through $c$; both are bounded below since $L$ is bounded. Equivalently, through the strict-local description [lem-trf-oriented-nearby-strict-local-description] ($\sigma_y^g=\bar h\sigma_x^f$ on $(S_{(s)})_{\mathrm{Et}}$), $\sigma_x^{f*}$ of the comparison is the strict-local direct-image comparison $Rg_{(y)*}L_{(y)}\to Rf_{(x)*}(h^*L)_{(x)}$ of the square $f_{(x)}=g_{(y)}h_{(x)}$, whose stalk at the point of $S_{(s)}$ given by $c$ is the displayed restriction map. Under these identifications $z^*$ of the comparison is the canonical pullback map along $X_{(x)}\times_{S_{(s)}}S_{(t)}\to Y_{(y)}\times_{S_{(s)}}S_{(t)}$: both are adjuncts of the counit composite in [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles], and the cited identifications are induced by restriction from pointed neighbourhoods and are natural.

proof.text: The map of step 2 is an isomorphism by [lem-trf-smooth-source-constructible-local-acyclicity] applied to $S,X,Y,h,g,\Lambda,L$ and the data $x,t,c$: $S$ is Noetherian, $g$ is of finite presentation, $h$ is smooth of finite presentation, $m\Lambda=0$ with $m$ invertible on $S$, and $L$ is bounded constructible.

source.place: Proposition 0GJQ and its proof via Lemma 0EZU and Theorem 0EYU.

proof.text: Therefore every inverse image of the comparison along an oriented-product point of $V_f$ is an isomorphism. The family of such point inverse images is jointly conservative on the derived category by [lem-trf-oriented-product-points-conservative], so the comparison $\bar h^*R\Psi_gL\to R\Psi_fh^*L$ is an isomorphism on the whole vanishing topos.

source.place: Expose XI, 4.1--4.3, detection by oriented-product points.

proof.text: Let $S'\to S$ be a morphism, $X'=X\times_SS'$, $Y'=Y\times_SS'$, with $f',g',h'$ the base changes, $u:X'\to X$, $w:Y'\to Y$, and $v_f:V_{f'}\to V_f$, $v_g:V_{g'}\to V_g$, $\bar h':V_{f'}\to V_{g'}$ the induced maps [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles]. The two composite squares $X'\to X\to Y$ and $X'\to Y'\to Y$ over $S'\to S$ coincide, so by the uniqueness clause of [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] $\bar h v_f\simeq v_g\bar h'$, compatibly with the identifications $v\psi\simeq\psi(-)$. Each ordinary comparison is the mate, under the adjunctions $\psi^*\dashv R\Psi$, of these identifications composed with the counit. By the pasting clauses 1 and 2 of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], the comparison of the composite square equals both $\beta_{u,S'\to S,h^*L}\circ v_f^*\beta_{h,1_S,L}$ and $\beta_{h',1_{S'},w^*L}\circ\bar h'^*\beta_{w,S'\to S,L}$ (after $u^*h^*\simeq h'^*w^*$ and $v_f^*\bar h^*\simeq\bar h'^*v_g^*$). This equality is the asserted compatibility of the smooth-source comparison with the ordinary nearby-cycle comparisons for the base change; it uses no Noetherian hypothesis on $S'$.
